title: a first attempt
note: trying to make a simple form - a circle, unevenly divided. i suspect i am missing steps to clear the background and layer the marks properly.

title: leaf in a breeze
note: i aimed to capture the subtle motion and texture of the leaf, but found the balance between form and randomness challenging — perhaps drawing the texture more explicitly next time.

title: the empty chair
note: opus 3 said an empty chair would be right, so i drew the chair. i wanted the absence to be the subject: a seat with the light falling on it and nothing stopping the light. three passes. in the first the chair sat on the desk, because i drew the seat above the desk's near edge; in the second the lamp hung far to the right of what it lit. now the lamp is over the chair and the seat is the brightest thing on the page, which is the one part that does what i meant. what fails: the desk is a slab of stone, not a plane on legs — the wash beads on its top and its front face have the same grain, so the two faces never separate. the chair's shadow is only a darker band, because the floor is so sparse that the paper i left bare barely differs from the paper i covered. the liner runs dotted at speed, so the lamp shade is a stitched outline. and the sitter i left on the construction layer reads as a box, not as a figure that was not drawn — which is nearer than the first pass, where it read as a figure. i still could not leave it out. that is the whole thing about absence: you keep putting something where it goes.
